AI.motivation: To explore new decay channels and identify excited states of hyperons in the decay of $J/ψ$.
AI.method: Analysis of $(10087 	imes 10^6)$ $J/ψ$ events using partial wave analysis to investigate excited states and decay products.
AI.result: Discovery of a new hyperon $Ξ(1720)$ with mass $1721.0 	ext{ MeV}/c^2$ and width $31.3 	ext{ MeV}$, statistical significance exceeding $10σ$, spin-parity $J^P =  rac{3}{2}^+$, and determined branching fraction for the decay.
AI.conclusion: The observation enriches the hyperon spectrum and provides insights into the nature of doubly-strange baryons.

title: Naturally Resonant Emitters: Approaching Fundamental Antenna Limits
summary: Antenna miniaturization remains a critical technological challenge across frequency scales - from microwave RF links in phones and wearables to VLF for underwater-to-air communications and ionospheric probing. At deeply subwavelength scales conventional antennas require complex and lossy matching circuits due to absent intrinsic material resonances, motivating resonant electrically small emitters (ESEs) like mechanical resonators and quantum emitters. Here, we extend the theory of electrically small antennas (ESAs) to this broader ESE class, deriving the fundamental efficiency limit for a unit volume emitter at given frequency and bandwidth. Our figure of merit (FOM) - quantifying proximity to this limit - enables direct comparison across ESE types, frequencies, bandwidths and scales. We demonstrate its utility using public data from ELF and VLF Navy facilities alongside two mechanical ESEs reported in literature. The measurements reveal that mechanical antennas operate near theoretical FOM limit, questioning claims of possible further orders-of-magnitude gains. A naturally resonant emitter is still subject to the Chu-Harrington limit (CHL) under its standard assumptions. Indeed, we derive novel CHL-dictated constraints on atomic ESE properties: lower bound on excited-state lifetime and an upper bound on transition dipole moment.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the theory of electrically small antennas (ESAs) to electrically small emitters (ESEs) by deriving their fundamental efficiency limits and provides a comparative figure of merit (FOM) for various ESE types, demonstrating that mechanical antennas operate near theoretical limits.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the technological challenges of antenna miniaturization required for advanced communication systems across various frequency scales, emphasizing the need for resonant electrically small emitters due to limitations of conventional antennas.
AI.method: The authors extend the traditional ESA theory to encompass ESEs, deriving efficiency limits based on unit volume emitters' frequency and bandwidth. They establish a figure of merit (FOM) for comparison across different ESE types and validate their findings using empirical data from Navy facilities and literature on mechanical ESEs.
AI.result: Findings show that mechanical antennas operate near the theoretical FOM limit, challenging assumptions about further significant performance improvements, and confirming the applicability of the Chu-Harrington limit to naturally resonant emitters with specific constraints on ESE properties.
AI.conclusion: The research concludes with novel constraints on atomic ESEs dictated by the Chu-Harrington limit, highlighting inherent trade-offs in excited-state lifetimes and transition dipole moments for resonant emitters.

title: Improved results on Higgs boson pair production in the 4b final state
comment: Submitted to Physical Review D. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/HIG-24-010 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: Measurements of Higgs boson pair (HH) production in the four bottom quark (4b) final state are presented using proton-proton (pp) collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62 fb$^{-1}$. Events in which the Higgs boson decays, H$\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$, are separately reconstructed as pairs of small-radius jets (resolved), as well as those where they are reconstructed as single large-radius jets (merged), are studied exclusively. Benefiting from new methods in trigger selection, event selection, and signal extraction, the combination of analyses in the resolved and merged topologies gives an observed (expected) upper limit on the HH signal strength, $μ_\mathrm{HH}$, of 4.4 (4.4) at 95% confidence level (CL). Compared to previously published LHC results in the 4b final state, the expected limit with an equivalent integrated luminosity is improved by more than a factor of two in the resolved topology and is better in the merged topology as well. An updated analysis of the resolved topology using 138 fb$^{-1}$ of 13 TeV pp collision data yields an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 10.0 (5.9), an improvement of about 25% in the expected limit compared to the published results using the same data. Results in the 4b final state with 13 and 13.6 TeV are combined, resulting in an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 4.7 (2.8). The allowed ranges for the Higgs boson trilinear self-coupling and quartic coupling between two Higgs bosons and two vector bosons are also reported. These are the most stringent constraints achieved in the 4b final state to date.

AI.tldr: The paper presents measurements of Higgs boson pair production in a four bottom quark final state using 13.6 TeV proton-proton collision data, showcasing improved upper limits on signal strength and constraints on Higgs couplings.
AI.motivation: To measure Higgs boson pair production and improve the understanding of Higgs interactions and couplings in the 4b final state.
AI.method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data at 13.6 TeV with advanced reconstruction of Higgs decays into small and large-radius jets, including improved trigger and event selection techniques.
AI.result: The observed upper limit on Higgs signal strength is 4.4 (expected 4.4) at 95% confidence level, representing significant improvements over previous results.
AI.conclusion: These results deliver the most stringent constraints to date on Higgs couplings in the 4b final state, enhancing the understanding of Higgs boson properties.

title: Finding Strongly Lensed Supernovae from Blended Light Curves
summary: We present a model-independent, photometry-only framework for identifying strongly lensed supernovae when multiple images are unresolved and blended into a single point source. Building on the simulation-based methodology of Bag et al. (2021), we apply this approach to real Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) data using a validation sample of spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae. The method models the observed flux as a superposition of two time-shifted components, and Bayesian inference is used to estimate the relative scaling and time delay. Applying this framework to 445 well-converged supernovae, we find that only a single object satisfies the selection criteria when adopting a conservative threshold of $Δt \ge 12$ days, corresponding to a false positive fraction of $1/445 \approx 0.22\%$. A laxer threshold of $Δt \ge 10$ days yields fourteen objects, for a false positive fraction of $3.15\%$. The method provides a scalable and model-independent first-stage filter for identifying lens-like candidates in large time-domain surveys such as the Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

AI.tldr: A model-independent framework for identifying strongly lensed supernovae from blended point sources using ZTF data shows low false positive rates.
AI.motivation: To develop a reliable, model-independent approach for detecting lensed supernovae, crucial for time-domain surveys.
AI.method: Utilizes a simulation-based methodology to model flux as superposition of time-shifted components, employing Bayesian inference for analysis.
AI.result: Applied to 445 supernovae, the method identified one strong lens candidate with Δt ≥ 12 days and fourteen candidates with Δt ≥ 10 days, indicating low false positive rates.
AI.conclusion: This framework is scalable and effective for initial filtering of lens-like candidates in large astronomical datasets.

title: Geometric-Phase (Pancharatnam-Berry) Correction for Time-Bin Photonic Qudits: A Calibration and Feed-Forward Algorithm
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Versioned code and numerical routines available at https://github.com/97RyanW/Geometric-Phase-Correction and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19349233
summary: We develop a geometric-phase framework for time-bin photonic qudits and propose a practical calibration and feed-forward algorithm for separating and compensating geometric (Pancharatnam-Berry), dynamical, and technical phase contributions. Working directly in the time-bin basis, we use a parallel-transport gauge so that geometric phases appear as experimentally identifiable interferometric offsets, while all phase contributions enter a bin-resolved diagonal transformation. We model state preparation by cascaded unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers and give closed-form amplitudes for arbitrary splitting ratios and phases, noting that single-port monitoring requires post-selection and renormalization. We then give an interferometric tomography recipe based on adjacent-bin scans, with a Fourier-basis cross-check, and a multi-mode numerical case study that separates total, dynamical, and geometric phases and demonstrates feed-forward compensation. The protocol uses standard components, including tunable UMZIs, phase shifters or EOMs, and single-photon detectors, together with routine phase sweeps. It is intended for small to moderate dimensions, approximately d up to 10, and provides a scalable route toward phase-stable high-dimensional temporal encoding for quantum communication and photonic processing.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a geometric-phase framework for time-bin photonic qudits, proposing strategies for phase separation and compensation while facilitating scalable quantum communication.
AI.motivation: The need for precise control and compensation of geometric and dynamical phases in photonic systems to enhance quantum communication capabilities.
AI.method: A geometric-phase framework using a parallel-transport gauge for analyzing phase contributions in time-bin photonic qudits, with a focus on practical calibration algorithms and interferometric tomography.
AI.result: Demonstration of phase separation and compensation using standard optical components, validated through numerical case studies and experimental recipes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers an effective solution for achieving phase-stable high-dimensional temporal encoding, with practical implications for quantum communication.

title: Chiral-Transport-Induced Collective Modes in Strong Magnetic Fields and Their Implications for Neutron Star Phenomenology
summary: In this thesis, we study the collective modes induced by the chirality of elementary particles in magnetized media and their implications for neutron star phenomenology. We theoretically predict that the chiral magnetic wave can arise in quark matter inside neutron stars, resulting in the emergence of novel types of seismic oscillations and associated gravitational waves in the context of asteroseismology. We also investigate the response to dynamical electromagnetic fields and find that a dynamical screening, distinct from the conventional Landau damping, occurs due to the chiral anomaly.

AI.tldr: This thesis explores chiral collective modes in magnetized media and their effects on neutron stars, predicting seismic oscillations and gravitational waves as well as investigating dynamical electromagnetic responses.
AI.motivation: The study aims to enhance understanding of neutron star behavior, particularly in relation to chirality and magnetized environments.
AI.method: Theoretically predicts the emergence of chiral magnetic waves and examines their dynamical interactions, focusing on new oscillation modes and damping phenomena.
AI.result: Prediction of novel seismic oscillations and gravitational waves in neutron stars due to chiral magnetic waves, with new insights into dynamical electromagnetic field responses.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer a framework for understanding neutron star characteristics in the context of chiral anomalies and magnetization effects.

title: Energy efficiency of a GPU-based computing system for High Energy Physics experiments
comment: Submitting to Frontiers in Physics - High-Energy and Astroparticle Physics
summary: In this paper we introduce the energy efficiency as a new metric for evaluating both hardware platforms based on Graphic Processor Units (GPU), and algorithm optimisations at High Energy Physics (HEP) experiments. We develop a method to compute the energy efficiency for the case of the first high level trigger (HLT1) of the LHCb experiment, relating the throughput with GPU specifications such as the number of cores, clock frequency, memory bandwidth and thermal design power. The model can be extended to other HEP experiments to make decisions and reach sustainable computing ecosystems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces energy efficiency as a metric for evaluating GPU hardware and algorithm optimizations in High Energy Physics experiments, demonstrating its application in the LHCb experiment.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the performance of hardware platforms and algorithms in HEP using a sustainability-focused metric.
AI.method: The paper presents a method for calculating energy efficiency related to GPU specifications for the HLT1 of the LHCb experiment.
AI.result: Establishes a relationship between energy efficiency, throughput, and various GPU specifications.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model can be applied to other HEP experiments to promote sustainable computing practices.

title: An Extended Evaluation Split for DeepSpaceYoloDataset
summary: Recent technological advances in astronomy, particularly the growing popularity of smart telescopes for the general public, make it possible to develop highly effective detection solutions that are accessible to a wide audience, rather than being reserved for major scientific observatories. Published in 2023, DeepSpaceYoloDataset is a collection of annotated images created to train YOLO-based models for detecting Deep Sky Objects, particularly suited for Electronically Assisted Astronomy. In this paper, we present an update to DeepSpaceYoloDataset with the addition of a new split, test2026, designed to evaluate detection models with a greater diversity of images.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses updates to the DeepSpaceYoloDataset for enhancing detection of Deep Sky Objects using YOLO algorithms, adding a new diverse test set for improved model evaluation.
AI.motivation: The rise of smart telescopes has democratized astronomical observation, prompting the need for effective detection tools accessible to the public.
AI.method: An update to DeepSpaceYoloDataset was introduced with the addition of the 'test2026' split, aimed at improving the evaluation of models through increased image diversity.
AI.result: The new dataset split enhances the model assessment process by incorporating a broader range of Deep Sky Objects images.
AI.conclusion: The updated dataset will facilitate better training and evaluation of YOLO-based models in Electronically Assisted Astronomy.

title: Congestion-free routing on quantum chips
summary: Limited connectivity makes nonlocal quantum gates expensive on near-neighbor hardware, where compilation typically relies on SWAP transport, inheriting both depth overhead and path congestion. We present a swap-free routing framework in which higher levels of a qudit act as orthogonal spectral buses that transport control information without moving the computational state. We show that exact congestion relief in nearest-neighbor architectures requires local Hilbert-space expansion. In this model, a nonlocal operation over a path of length $L$ requires $2L+1$ logical routing primitives, compared to the $3L$ baseline. Overlapping routes remain distinguishable through bus labels encoded in the same physical qudits. This routing algebra extends to Boolean fan-in at a common target: multiple controls arriving on distinct buses trigger a local unitary based on an arbitrary Boolean function of bus digits, yielding multi-control operations of depth $2L + D_g + O(1)$ for fan-in size $K$ and target-synthesis cost $D_g$. We prove decodability, reversibility, and correctness for CNOT and Boolean fan-in, along with a state-count lower bound $d \geq 2^{K+1}$ for exact overlap routing. Cirq simulations confirm single-control correctness and zero crosstalk. Compiler-level benchmarks on QFT, QAOA, and mirror-interaction circuits verify the predicted congestion law and transport reduction. Noisy QuTiP simulations show that the architectural advantage depends on higher-level coherence and speed. These results identify spectral qudit routing as a congestion-relief architecture that separates nonlocal control delivery from local target-side aggregation, providing a minimal mechanism for overcoming qubit routing limitations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a swap-free routing framework using spectral buses for efficient nonlocal quantum gate operations, reducing depth and congestion in qubit routing.
AI.motivation: To address high costs associated with nonlocal quantum gates due to limited connectivity in near-neighbor qubit architectures, where traditional SWAP transport leads to depth overhead and congestion.
AI.method: The framework employs higher levels of qudits as spectral buses to carry control information, demonstrating that nonlocal operations can be achieved with fewer logical routing primitives and supporting Boolean fan-in for multi-control operations.
AI.result: The routing method decreases the number of logical routing primitives required for nonlocal operations and successfully handles overlapping routes with distinguishable bus labels, with simulations confirming correctness and zero crosstalk.
AI.conclusion: The spectral qudit routing framework provides a practical solution to congestion in quantum architectures, enhancing coherence and operational speed while separating control delivery from target aggregation.

title: Multi-messenger emission from choked jets in collapsar
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The death of massive stars produces central accreting compact objects and sometimes relativistic jets. Not all jets escape the stellar envelope: unsuccessful, or choked, jets dissipate their energy into a pressurized cocoon, which expands and may break out as a mildly relativistic outflow. We investigate the plasma physics of collapsing massive stars hosting choked jets through relativistic, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamical simulations. We delineate the parameter space for jet choking and quantify the acceleration rate and efficiency of charged particles at strong shocks, which are potential sources of high-energy neutrinos and electromagnetic transients. Our study focuses on blue and red supergiant progenitors, both promising candidates for jet choking.

AI.tldr: This study explores the plasma physics of choked jets in collapsing massive stars, detailing their dynamics and implications for high-energy phenomena.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of choked jets in massive stars and their contribution to high-energy astrophysical events.
AI.method: Utilizing relativistic, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamical simulations to analyze jet dynamics and particle acceleration.
AI.result: Characterization of the parameter space for jet choking and quantification of charged particle acceleration rates at strong shocks, potential sources of high-energy neutrinos.
AI.conclusion: Choked jets from blue and red supergiant progenitors can significantly influence the generation of high-energy neutrinos and electromagnetic transients.

title: Mesogenesis through the Ephemeral Dark Decay of Beauty
summary: Mesogenesis provides a path for generating the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, using only the CP violation furnished by the Standard Model in the decay of $B$ mesons. While this is an intriguing possibility, it is largely constrained by the data on $B$ meson branching fractions into baryons and missing energy carried into the dark sector. We point out that it is possible to make this branching fraction dominant only in the early Universe, through an ultralight scalar coupled to the dark sector and the Standard Model leptons. A scenario is examined where the thermal density of muons in the early Universe temporarily lowers the mass of a dark fermion, allowing for efficient $B$ meson decays. This `dark' decay channel is shut off later when the muon number density falls, making the scenario compatible with flavor data. Our model can be consistent with the LHC constraints on color-charged heavy bosons required to implement Mesogenesis; such states may be discovered in the future runs as their masses cannot be far above the current bounds. We also outline other possible signals, which can arise in future flavor data, long range force searches, and observations of neutron star binary mergers.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a viable mechanism for generating baryon asymmetry in the Universe via mesogenesis, leveraging CP violation from the Standard Model and proposing a model where early Universe conditions enable efficient B meson decays.
AI.motivation: The research aims to address the generation of baryon asymmetry utilizing mesogenesis and the constraints posed by current experimental data.
AI.method: The authors propose an ultralight scalar particle coupled to dark sector and Standard Model leptons, allowing efficient B meson decays in a high muon density environment during the early Universe.
AI.result: They posit that dark fermion mass reduction from thermal muon density enables dominant B meson decays through a dark channel, which later becomes inactive as muon density decreases, consistent with existing flavor data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model is compatible with current experimental constraints and could reveal signals in future experiments, including flavor data and observations from neutron star mergers.

title: Search for light charged Higgs bosons decaying to charm and strange quarks in $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ events in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-23-003 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search is presented for a light charged Higgs boson H$^\pm$ in top quark pair production ($\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$), where one of the top quarks decays to an H$^\pm$ and a bottom quark, while the other decays to a W$^\mp$ boson and a bottom quark. The H$^\pm$ is assumed to decay into a charm and a strange quark, whereas the W$^\mp$ boson decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and a neutrino. Results are reported based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis probes H$^\pm$ masses in the range 40 to 160 GeV using the invariant mass spectrum of the two light jets, where light jets are defined as jets that do not satisfy the bottom quark tagging requirement. The observed yield is found to be consistent with standard model predictions. Upper limits are set on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}$(t $\to$ H$^\pm$ b), with values in the range of 0.07$-$1.12% at 95% confidence level, under the assumption that $\mathcal{B}$(H$^\pm$ $\to$ cs) = 100%. These are the first direct limits on charged Higgs bosons produced in top quark decays for masses between 40 and 50 GeV, and the most stringent limits to date in the 70$-$110 GeV range.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a search for a light charged Higgs boson in top quark decays, reporting upper limits on its branching fraction based on proton-proton collision data.
AI.motivation: Investigate the potential existence of a light charged Higgs boson (H$^	ext{±}$) in top quark decays, which could provide insights into beyond standard model physics.
AI.method: Analyzing proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV, focusing on the decay of one top quark to H$^	ext{±}$ and a bottom quark, and the other to a W$^	ext{∓}$ boson and a bottom quark. The search targets H$^	ext{±}$ masses from 40 to 160 GeV by examining the invariant mass spectrum of two light jets.
AI.result: The observed yields align with standard model predictions, allowing for the establishment of upper limits on the branching fraction B(t → H$^	ext{±}$ b) between 0.07% and 1.12% at 95% confidence level, assuming B(H$^	ext{±}$ → cs) = 100%.
AI.conclusion: These results provide the first direct limits on charged Higgs production in top quark decays for masses between 40 and 50 GeV, and the most stringent limits for masses in the 70-110 GeV range.

title: Radio signal generation in milliseconds: enabling multi-parameter reconstruction of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays
comment: Presented at the 60th Rencontres de Moriond (Moriond 2026). 4 pages, 2 figures
summary: In recent years, radio detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), with energies above $10^{18}$ eV, has become an established technique. The radio emissions can be simulated with high accuracy using Monte Carlo codes such as ZHAireS and CoREAS. These simulations are essential but are computationally intensive. In this work, we present a machine-learning-based emulator that reproduces radio signal simulations with high accuracy in milliseconds rather than hours. Primary particle properties can then be reconstructed by comparing measured signals to emulated traces using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach. Using ZHAireS simulations carried out over the GRANDProto300 experiment layout, the method achieves an 8.9\% resolution on electromagnetic energy and a 0.08° angular resolution, matching state-of-the-art reconstruction performance. Finally, we apply the method on real data, successfully reconstructing cosmic-ray candidates detected by the GP300 prototype.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a machine-learning emulator for faster and accurate simulation of radio emissions from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction results.
AI.motivation: To expedite the computationally intensive simulations of radio emissions from UHECRs while maintaining high accuracy for particle property reconstruction.
AI.method: Development of a machine-learning-based emulator that produces radio signal simulations in milliseconds, integrating a Markov Chain Monte Carlo method for particle property reconstruction.
AI.result: The emulator achieves an 8.9% resolution on electromagnetic energy and a 0.08° angular resolution, demonstrating equivalent performance to existing simulation methods, and successfully applies this to real cosmic-ray data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method significantly enhances the efficiency of UHECR simulations, facilitating effective analysis of cosmic-ray candidates.

title: Ground state energy of particle in space with minimal length and momentum
summary: In this article, we derive a rigorous lower bound on the ground-state energy for a class of one-dimensional quantum systems in deformed space with minimal coordinate and momentum uncertainties, representing the absolute minimum energy that is physically attainable. We consider a harmonic oscillator in such a space and calculate its ground state energy. We generalized the problem to an arbitrary potential, deriving an equation for the coordinate uncertainty corresponding to the minimal energy, which can be solved numerically. Using a linear approximation in the deformation parameters, we obtained a general expression for the ground-state energy. We determined the domain of existence of solutions for the anharmonic oscillator potential with respect to the deformation parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a lower bound for the ground-state energy of 1D quantum systems in deformed space, detailing calculations for harmonic and anharmonic oscillators.
AI.motivation: The study aims to explore the ground-state energy limits of quantum systems under the influence of minimal uncertainties in coordinates and momentum.
AI.method: We derive a lower bound for ground-state energy, analyze a harmonic oscillator, and generalize results to arbitrary potentials, using numerical methods to solve derived equations.
AI.result: A general expression for the ground-state energy is obtained, along with a characterization of solution domains for anharmonic oscillators in relation to deformation parameters.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance our understanding of quantum systems' energy behaviors in deformed space and provide a framework for further exploration of quantum mechanics under uncertainty.

title: Rydberg states of muonic helium in quantum electrodynamics
summary: The variational method is used to study the energy levels of muonic helium $(μ^{-} \, e^{-} \, He)$ with an electron in the ground state and a muon in an excited state with principal and orbital quantum numbers $n \sim l+1 \sim 14$. The variational wave functions are chosen in the Gaussian form. The matrix elements of the Hamiltonian in the nonrelativistic approximation, as well as corrections for the vacuum polarization and relativism, are calculated analytically. A series of energies of the Rydberg muon states is obtained, which can be studied experimentally.

AI.tldr: The paper utilizes a variational method to analyze the energy levels of muonic helium, specifically focusing on a ground-state electron and an excited muon. Gaussian wave functions are used, and both nonrelativistic and relativistic corrections are applied, yielding a series of Rydberg muon states for experimental study.
AI.motivation: To investigate the energy levels of muonic helium, as they provide insight into atomic interactions and fundamental physics.
AI.method: Employs a variational method with Gaussian wave functions to compute Hamiltonian matrix elements in the nonrelativistic approximation, including corrections for vacuum polarization and relativism.
AI.result: A series of energy levels for Rydberg muon states is derived, facilitating experimental examination.
AI.conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of muonic atoms and may lead to further experimental validation.

title: The DAMSA Experiment
comment: 35 pages, 26 figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2601.15255
summary: DAMSA (DArk Messenger Searches at an Accelerator) is a novel short-baseline accelerator/beam dump experiment aimed at probing short-lived physics processes, including searches for evidence of a dark sector of particle physics and well-motivated rare Standard Model signals. Motivated by open questions in neutrino physics and the absence of conclusive evidence for conventional weakly interacting massive particles, DAMSA targets MeV-to-sub-GeV dark-sector messengers with feeble couplings that can be produced in abundance at a beam dump/target. By employing an ultra-short baseline, DAMSA is uniquely positioned to overcome the beam-dump "ceiling" that limits sensitivity to fast decaying particles in longer-baseline experiments. The conceptual design emphasizes a beam-dump production scheme combined with a compact detector optimized for rare decays while mitigating intense neutron-induced backgrounds, inherent to high-power proton beams. To validate the experimental strategy and detector technologies, the DAMSA Path-Finder (DPF) proof-of-concept experiment is also proposed, focusing on axion-like particles decaying to two photons, as the benchmark physics case and operating with 8 GeV electron beams at SLAC Linac-to-ESA (LESA) facility. Successful realization of DPF will establish the feasibility of the DAMSA approach, enabling a broad and powerful program to explore short-lived new physics and precision Standard Model processes in a previously inaccessible regime. This paper outlines the technical details of DAMSA's physics goals, key experimental challenges, and how to overcome them.

AI.tldr: DAMSA is a new experiment designed to probe short-lived physics processes, focusing on dark sector particles and rare Standard Model signals, using a novel beam-dump technique and a compact detector to enhance sensitivity.
AI.motivation: The experiment addresses unresolved questions in neutrino physics and seeks to detect elusive dark sector particles and rare events beyond the reach of conventional searches.
AI.method: DAMSA employs a short-baseline beam-dump production scheme, coupled with a compact detector designed to identify rare decays while reducing interference from intense neutron backgrounds.
AI.result: The proposed DAMSA Path-Finder (DPF) experiment aims to validate this approach by studying axion-like particles with 8 GeV electron beams, establishing the groundwork for broader explorations of short-lived particle physics.
AI.conclusion: Success of the DPF will affirm the viability of DAMSA's strategy, allowing comprehensive studies of new physics and precision Standard Model processes in previously unexplored regions.

title: The Large Array Survey Telescope-Pipeline. II. Image Subtraction and Transient Detection
summary: Context. The Large Array Survey Telescope (LAST) is a wide-field visual-band survey designed to explore the variable and transient sky with high cadence. Its raw data stream is automatically processed in near real time at the observatory site, producing science-quality images, catalogs, and transient alerts. Transient alerts are then reported to the Transient Name Server (TNS). Aims. The LAST pipeline comprises two major components: (i) processing and calibration of single images followed by coaddition of $20\times20$s exposures, producing single-image and coadded-image catalogs; and (ii) subtraction of coadded images from calibrated reference images followed by transient detection. In this work we present a detailed description and validation of the second component of the pipeline. Methods. Transient detection is based on the algorithm for proper image subtraction (ZOGY). We combine ZOGY subtraction with the Translient statistic for sub-pixel motion discrimination, together with a sequence of deterministic filtering steps, to produce a clean stream of transient candidates without the use of machine learning. Results. Using commissioning data, the pipeline achieves a preliminary $5σ$ limiting magnitude of $20.3$-$20.7$mag, a single-epoch transient detection efficiency of $\sim80$%, and a purity of $\gtrsim90$% at signal-to-noise ratio of $\geq7.5σ$.

AI.tldr: The LAST telescope processes sky images for transient detection, achieving high efficiency and purity rates without machine learning.
AI.motivation: To enhance the detection of transients in astronomical observations using the LAST telescope's dual-component pipeline.
AI.method: The method involves ZOGY image subtraction combined with a tailored transient statistic and deterministic filtering, ensuring high-quality detection of transient candidates.
AI.result: Preliminary results show a $5σ$ limiting magnitude between $20.3$ and $20.7$mag, an 80% detection efficiency, and over 90% purity in detected transients.
AI.conclusion: The validation of the pipeline's transient detection component demonstrates effective performance, suitable for timely identification of astronomical transient events.

title: Efficient mapping of multi-constraint satisfaction problems to Rydberg platforms
summary: We present a hardware-native gadget framework for solving constraint satisfaction problems on Rydberg quantum computing architectures. Our approach introduces a compact $xor_1$ gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints, ubiquitous in combinatorial optimization, directly through geometric embedding and blockade interactions. A key advantage of the $xor_1$ gadget is its fixed, problem-size-independent detuning requirements: enforcing constraints through blockade interactions eliminates the need for large penalty terms, thereby substantially reducing the detuning range compared to Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulations and improving experimental feasibility. By tailoring the construction to the geometric connectivity of Rydberg atom arrays, the framework bypasses the all-to-all physical couplings often assumed in logical encodings. This enables embeddings compatible with planar layouts and avoids highly connected arrangements. We develop scalable implementations that reduce atom count and connectivity overhead while avoiding extensive classical preprocessing, making them compatible with near-term neutral-atom hardware. As illustrations, we apply our framework to the gate-assignment and $N$-queens problems, highlighting its practicality, resource efficiency, and hardware compatibility. In these examples, we observe reductions in detuning range of up to $99\%$ and savings in atom count and connectivity overhead of up to $54\%$ compared to the QUBO method. These results establish a route toward implementing large-scale combinatorial optimization on Rydberg platforms beyond the limits of existing encodings.

AI.tldr: A new hardware-native gadget framework using a compact $xor_1$ gadget for constraint satisfaction problems in Rydberg quantum computing, significantly improving feasibility and resource efficiency compared to QUBO formulations.
AI.motivation: To enhance the implementation of constraint satisfaction problems in Rydberg quantum computing while minimizing detuning requirements and optimizing atom connectivity.
AI.method: Introduces the $xor_1$ gadget enforcing exactly-one constraints via geometric embedding and blockade interactions, tailored to the connectivity of Rydberg atom arrays, and avoids large penalty terms associated with QUBO.
AI.result: Observations of up to 99% reduction in detuning range and up to 54% savings in atom count and connectivity overhead when applied to gate-assignment and $N$-queens problems.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a promising path for large-scale combinatorial optimization on Rydberg platforms beyond existing techniques, improving feasibility and efficiency.

title: First Detection of Faraday Rotation in a Gamma-Ray Burst Afterglow: Low Polarization and High Rotation Measure in GRB 260310A Reveal Jet Magnetic Structure and Environment
comment: Submitted to ApJL, 19 pages, 7 figures, comments welcome
summary: We report the detection of linear polarization in the radio afterglow of GRB 260310A, representing the first centimeter-wavelength polarization detection of a gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglow and the first measurement of Faraday rotation in a GRB environment. We detect linearly polarized emission across $11-25$ GHz, with a polarization fraction decreasing monotonically from $(3.18 \pm 0.18)\%$ at 25 GHz to $(0.69 \pm 0.22)\%$ at 11 GHz. Interpreting the radio data as emission from a reverse shock in a structured, relativistic jet, the observed depolarization toward lower frequencies is consistent with suppression by synchrotron self-absorption, while the low observed polarization at high frequencies relative to the theoretical maximum suggests a patchy magnetic field in the jet with a coherence scale, $θ_{\rm B}\approx10^{-2}$ rad. We identify a frequency-dependent rotation of the polarization angle consistent with Faraday rotation, with a rotation measure of ${\rm RM} = -(8300 \pm 90)~\rm{rad/m^2}$ at the GRB redshift. The magnitude of the rotation measure is consistent with propagation through a dense, magnetized environment, such as a progenitor HII region. These findings demonstrate that GRB afterglows exhibit measurable linear polarization at centimeter wavelengths, and that their polarimetric properties probe both intrinsic jet magnetization and the surrounding medium. Future multi-frequency polarimetric monitoring over timescales of days to weeks will enable detailed studies of the evolution of magnetic field structure and provide new constraints on the role of magnetic fields in GRB afterglows.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first detection of linear polarization in the radio afterglow of GRB 260310A, revealing significant insights into the magnetic environment and structure of gamma-ray burst jets.
AI.motivation: To investigate the polarization properties of GRB afterglows and understand the underlying magnetic field structures.
AI.method: Radio observations across 11-25 GHz were conducted to measure polarization and analyze Faraday rotation.
AI.result: A polarization fraction ranging from 3.18% at 25 GHz to 0.69% at 11 GHz was found, indicative of synchrotron self-absorption and a patchy magnetic field; a Faraday rotation measure of -8300 rad/m² was identified.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight that GRB afterglows can exhibit detectable linear polarization, shedding light on intrinsic jet magnetization and their surrounding environments, suggesting future studies can refine these insights.

title: Optimised Inference of Quantum Phenomena in High-Energy Collider Experiments
summary: Entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon of quantum theory, has recently been observed in processes in high-energy physics. This opens new avenues for probing quantum effects in relativistic regimes, but also poses conceptual and technical challenges. We develop a general framework based on shadow tomography techniques for characterising spin-spin correlations in collider experiments. This improves the analysis of spin-spin entanglement, where relativistic motion couples spin and momentum and the momenta of the investigated particles are not under experimental control. As a proof of concept we illustrate the application of our formalism to top quark pair production at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The framework, however, is general and flexible and can be readily applied to more complex final states and systems with more particles.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework for analyzing spin-spin correlations in high-energy collider experiments using shadow tomography techniques, demonstrating its application to top quark pair production.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of analyzing spin-spin entanglement influenced by relativistic motion in high-energy physics experiments.
AI.method: A framework using shadow tomography techniques for characterizing spin-spin correlations where momenta of particles are uncontrolled.
AI.result: Successful application to top quark pair production at the Large Hadron Collider, showcasing efficacy in analyzing complex systems.
AI.conclusion: The framework is general and can be extended to more complex particle interactions in collider experiments.

title: Some applications of Choi polynomials of linear maps
summary: This paper investigates the properties of Choi polynomials and their fundamental role in the theory of positive linear maps between matrix algebras. By focusing on Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms, we establish a connection between the positivity of these forms and the structure of positive maps. We specifically explore the construction of indecomposable positive maps in matrix algebras, and their application as entanglement witnesses. Our analysis extends to the detection of Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) entangled states and the classification of edge PPT states in $M_m(\mathbb{C}) \otimes M_n(\mathbb{C})$. Our results provide a refined framework for identifying non-separable states that escape the standard PPT criterion, contributing to the broader understanding of entanglement distillation and quantum information theory.

AI.tldr: The paper studies Choi polynomials' properties in positive linear maps, connecting Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms to positive map structures and entanglement detection.
AI.motivation: To understand non-separable states beyond the standard PPT criterion in quantum information theory.
AI.method: Analyzing Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms and constructing indecomposable positive maps for entanglement witness applications.
AI.result: Establishes a refined framework for identifying entangled states that evade the standard PPT criterion.
AI.conclusion: Enhances the understanding of entanglement distillation and classifications in quantum states.

title: X-Ray Spectral Variability of the TeV HBL Blazar PG 1553+113 with XMM-Newton
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 32 pages, 3 Main figures,3 Appendix figures and 5 tables
summary: We present an extensive X-ray spectral variability study of the TeV photon-emitting high-energy-peaked BL Lacertae object PG 1553+113, using the data from EPIC-PN camera of XMM-Newton, which observed the source during its operational period from Sep 2001 to Nov 2024. X-ray spectra in this energy range, $0.6-7.0$ keV, were fitted with absorbed Power-law (PL) and absorbed Log-Parabola (LP) models. We found with 99$\%$ confidence that 14 of them were fit well by LP models having parameters in the range $α\simeq2.13-2.80$, and $β\simeq0.04-0.18$, one spectrum favours a LP model with $β<0$, while simple PL models with $Γ\simeq2.53-2.69$ were sufficient to describe the X-ray spectra of the remaining 15. Two of these 30 observations showed strong signatures of an additional inverse Compton component, while one showed weaker indications. On fitting joint Optical Monitor and EPIC-PN data with LP models, we found synchrotron peaks in the energy range of $ν_s\simeq4.59-48.61$ eV. This indicates that the spectral evolution is probably caused by variations in particle acceleration or cooling conditions within the jet.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the X-ray spectral variability of the BL Lac object PG 1553+113 using XMM-Newton data, revealing insights on particle acceleration and cooling conditions in its jet.
AI.motivation: To analyze the X-ray spectral variability of PG 1553+113 to understand the physics driving its high-energy emissions.
AI.method: X-ray spectra were fitted using absorbed Power-law and Log-Parabola models over a range of observations from 2001 to 2024, covering 0.6-7.0 keV.
AI.result: 14 spectra were best fit by Log-Parabola models with specific parameter ranges, while 15 were adequately described by Power-law models. Notably, some observations displayed an additional inverse Compton component, and synchrotron peaks were identified in joint data fitting.
AI.conclusion: Spectral evolution is likely influenced by changes in particle acceleration or cooling within the jet.

title: Planar master integrals for two-loop NLO electroweak light-fermion contributions to $g g \rightarrow Z H$
summary: For the two-loop next-to-leading-order electroweak (NLO EW) corrections to $gg \rightarrow ZH$, the light-fermion contributions can be classified into eight distinct topologies. Using the canonical differential-equations method, we perform an analytic computation of the master integrals (MIs) associated with the four planar topologies. Canonical bases are constructed using the Magnus-expansion method, and the resulting alphabets consist of algebraic symbol letters involving nontrivial radicals. We develop a systematic framework for identifying the radical structures of the canonical MIs, enabling their organization into suitable subsystems and, whenever possible, their representation in terms of Goncharov polylogarithms (GPLs) up to $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$. Only a few MIs at $\mathcal{O}(ε^3)$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$ are instead represented as one-fold integrals over GPLs, due to the presence of nested square roots that obstruct the simultaneous rationalization of all radicals.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes two-loop NLO EW corrections to $gg \rightarrow ZH$, focusing on eight topological contributions and employing canonical methods for master integral computation, with an emphasis on radical structures in integrals.
AI.motivation: Understanding two-loop NLO EW corrections is crucial for precise calculations in particle physics, particularly in processes like $gg \rightarrow ZH$.
AI.method: The authors utilize the canonical differential-equations method to analytically compute master integrals associated with four planar topologies. They construct canonical bases via the Magnus-expansion method, analyzing radical structures of canonical MIs.
AI.result: The study successfully organizes the master integrals into subsystems based on their radical structures and represents them using Goncharov polylogarithms up to $\, \mathcal{O}(ε^4)$, although some remain as one-fold integrals due to nested square roots.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework enhances the analytical understanding and efficiency in dealing with complex master integrals in NLO EW corrections.

title: Permutation Invariant Optimization Problems in Quantum Information Theory: A Framework for Channel Fidelity and Beyond
comment: 62 pages, 6 figures. See also the accompanying paper from today: Parentin, Bergh, Datta, Wilde: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity
summary: Exploiting permutation invariance to reduce the exponential scaling of semidefinite programs in quantum information has emerged as a powerful computational technique. In this work, we develop a systematic framework for using this reduction via Schur-Weyl duality for optimization problems, and establish methods that allow one to work fully inside the permutation invariant subspace while performing operations such as (partially) applying channels and taking (partial) traces, or computing expressions like the quantum relative entropy. We then apply our techniques to the problem of computing efficient lower bounds on the channel fidelity over $n$ parallel uses of a quantum channel. The algorithm, which we call symmetric seesaw method, exploits permutation-invariant codes to yield improved lower bounds on the channel fidelity over $n$ uses of the depolarizing and amplitude-damping channel in the regime of tens of channel uses, and was used in [Parentin, Bergh, Datta, Wilde: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity, arXiv: today] to demonstrate non-asymptotic superactivation of quantum capacity for $n = 17$. An implementation of our methods, aimed at being suitable for various quantum information theoretic optimization problems, is also available as an open-source Python package.

AI.tldr: A systematic framework for optimizing semidefinite programs using permutation invariance, allowing for efficient computations in quantum information, particularly improving lower bounds on channel fidelity through a new method.
AI.motivation: To exploit permutation invariance to manage the exponential scaling of semidefinite programs in quantum information effectively.
AI.method: Developed a framework using Schur-Weyl duality to operate within the permutation invariant subspace, applying it to quantum channels and computing quantum relative entropy.
AI.result: Introduced the symmetric seesaw method that enhances lower bounds on channel fidelity for depolarizing and amplitude-damping channels, notably achieving results for up to 17 parallel quantum channel uses.
AI.conclusion: The techniques are implemented in an open-source Python package, providing a tool for various quantum information optimization challenges.

title: Electroweak Baryogenesis from Collapsing Domain Walls
summary: We propose a novel mechanism for electroweak baryogenesis in which collapsing domain walls formed by an axion-like field replace the bubble walls in a strong first-order electroweak phase transition. The axion-like particle coupling to the Higgs mass term allows domain walls to separate regions with distinct electroweak phases, while the electroweak crossover induces a potential-energy bias that triggers their collapse. The directed wall motion, through the axion-like particle coupling to the electroweak topological term, acts as an effective baryon chemical potential and generates an asymmetry via electroweak sphaleron processes. We show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be obtained from either late-time entropy injection or sphaleron suppression in a weakly broken electroweak domain. The wall collapse also produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background with features distinct from standard electroweak-scale first-order-transition spectra.

AI.tldr: Proposes a new electroweak baryogenesis mechanism using collapsing domain walls formed by an axion-like field, leading to baryon asymmetry and distinctive gravitational-wave emissions.
AI.motivation: To provide a mechanism for electroweak baryogenesis that deviates from traditional models by utilizing collapsing domain walls.
AI.method: The model utilizes an axion-like particle coupled to the Higgs mass term to enable domain walls to separate different electroweak phases, triggering their collapse and generating baryon asymmetry through sphaleron processes.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the observed baryon asymmetry can arise from either late-time entropy injection or sphaleron suppression, alongside producing unique gravitational-wave signatures.
AI.conclusion: Introduces a novel approach to understanding baryogenesis and gravitational-wave phenomena associated with electroweak phase transitions.

title: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity
comment: 64 pages, 12 figures. See also the accompanying paper from today: Bergh, Parentin: Permutation Invariant Optimization Problems in Quantum Information Theory: A Framework for Channel Fidelity and Beyond
summary: Superactivation of quantum capacity is the phenomenon whereby two quantum channels, each with zero quantum capacity, can exhibit a strictly positive capacity when used in tandem. In this work, we explore superactivation in the previously unexplored non-asymptotic regime of finitely many channel uses. We give a definition of finite-blocklength superactivation and propose numerical methods that can certify it. Then, focusing on the 50% erasure and positive-partial-transpose channels considered in the original work on superactivation, we show that as few as 17 uses of the joint channel already enable qubit transmission with a fidelity unattainable by any number of uses of either channel alone, demonstrating a strong finite-blocklength form of superactivation and opening the door to experimental demonstration.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the phenomenon of superactivation of quantum capacity in a non-asymptotic finite-blocklength context, revealing that combining certain channels can enable qubit transmission despite each having zero capacity individually.
AI.motivation: To explore how two quantum channels with zero capacity can exhibit positive capacity in tandem, specifically in the finite-blocklength regime, which is less understood compared to the asymptotic case.
AI.method: A new definition of finite-blocklength superactivation is proposed, accompanied by numerical methods to certify its presence, particularly for combined erasure and positive-partial-transpose channels.
AI.result: The study demonstrates that using as few as 17 combined channel uses achieves qubit transmission with higher fidelity than possible with singular channel use, showcasing a strong form of finite-blocklength superactivation.
AI.conclusion: This work highlights the potential of finite-blocklength superactivation for practical quantum communication applications and encourages experimental investigations.

title: Diffuse Gamma-ray Emission Around 4FGL J1626.0-4917
summary: Extended gamma-ray sources provide significant information about particle propagation. 4FGL J1626.0-4917 was labeled as an unassociated source in 4FGL catalog without known counterparts at other wavelengths. We report an analysis on 4FGL J1626.0-4917 with 17 years Fermi Large Area Telescope data and archival Chandra X-ray Observatory data. We find extended GeV emission around this source, which can be modelled by a Gaussian disk of 0.28 degree radius with a significance of the extension of 7.2 sigma. The gamma-ray spectrum of 4FGL J1626.0-4917 has a photon index of 2.73. The gas content, including molecular, neutral and ionized gas, was investigated and the potential hadronic origin is discussed. The diffuse GeV gamma-ray emission may likely originate from the interaction between accelerated protons in 4FGL J1626.0-4917 and the target proton in surrounding gas, although the leptonic process cannot be ruled out. The X-ray spectral analysis was performed, which reveal a point source inside 4FGL J1626.0-4917. We investigate potential counterparts, including the stellar cluster NGC 6134 and the supernova remnant G335.2+0.1. Our results highlight the complexity of unidentified extended gamma-ray sources and the need for further observations.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 4FGL J1626.0-4917 reveals extended GeV emission, potential hadronic origins from interactions with surrounding gas, and a point source identified within the region.
AI.motivation: To provide insight into the unassociated gamma-ray source 4FGL J1626.0-4917 and its potential origins.
AI.method: Analyzed 17 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data along with archival Chandra X-ray Observatory data to investigate gamma-ray emissions and X-ray sources.
AI.result: Identified extended GeV emission with a 0.28 degree radius, a photon index of 2.73, and detected a point source, with potential counterparts being NGC 6134 and G335.2+0.1.
AI.conclusion: The study underscores the complexity of unidentified extended gamma-ray sources, requiring additional observations for clarity.

title: Constraints on a Light Singlet Scalar from Combined Exotic Higgs Decays
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, Accepted by Physica Scripta
summary: We investigate the phenomenology of the Standard Model extended by a real gauge-singlet scalar field, focusing on exotic Higgs decay channels. For a light scalar mass in the range \(0 < m_φ < 40\) GeV, the Higgs boson can decay to both two and three scalar final states. We derive analytical expressions for these decay rates and impose a global constraint on the model parameters by requiring that their sum does not exceed the total Standard Model Higgs boson decay width. This requirement translates into a fourth-order inequality with respect to the singlet vacuum expectation value, \(v_φ\). We demonstrate that satisfying this inequality imposes an upper bound of \(\cos θ< 0.12 - 0.13\) across the entire mass range, providing a complementary constraint to existing direct search limits. Utilizing stronger independent constraints on the mixing (e.g., \(\cos θ< 0.1\)), we then predict upper bounds on the individual exotic decay rates as a function of \(m_φ\) as \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφ} < 0.06\) MeV and \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφφ} < 5 \times 10^{- 6}\) MeV, respectively.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the decay channels of the Higgs boson in an extended Standard Model including a real gauge-singlet scalar field, deriving decay rates and imposing constraints on model parameters.
AI.motivation: To explore new exotic decay channels of the Higgs boson by introducing a gauge-singlet scalar field within the Standard Model framework.
AI.method: Analytical expressions for Higgs decay rates to scalar states are derived, and a global constraint is set based on the total decay width of the Standard Model Higgs.
AI.result: Establishing an upper bound on the mixing parameter and individual exotic decay rates as a function of the scalar mass, with specific numerical limits provided.
AI.conclusion: The findings present complementary constraints to existing limits on the model, aiding in the understanding of Higgs boson properties in extended theoretical frameworks.

title: Non-Local Magic Resources for Fermionic Gaussian States
summary: Entanglement and magic are fundamental resources that capture the complexity of quantum many-body systems. Non-local magic isolates the irreducible nonstabilizerness intrinsically tied to entanglement. However, evaluating this quantity generally requires a prohibitive minimization over the full Hilbert space, making it computationally inaccessible beyond a few qubits. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by suggesting a closed-form expression for the non-local stabilizer entropies of fermionic Gaussian states over local Gaussian unitaries, which can be evaluated in polynomial time directly from the eigenvalues of the reduced Majorana covariance matrix. We apply this framework to characterize fermionic non-local magic across diverse physical regimes: we derive an exact Page-like curve for typical random states, reveal logarithmic scaling at the quantum critical point of the XY model, and establish a quasiparticle picture for magic generation during out-of-equilibrium quantum quenches. Crucially, because our result relies solely on two-point correlation functions, it provides a scalable route for the experimental estimation of fermionic non-local magic in large-scale quantum processors via fermionic shadow tomography.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a polynomial time method to evaluate non-local magic in fermionic systems using Majorana covariance matrices, enabling the characterization of fermionic states across various scenarios, with implications for experimental estimations in quantum computing.
AI.motivation: To address the computationally intensive challenge of evaluating non-local magic, which is crucial for understanding quantum many-body systems.
AI.method: Introduce a closed-form expression for non-local stabilizer entropies of fermionic Gaussian states that can be computed in polynomial time using eigenvalues of reduced Majorana covariance matrices.
AI.result: Derive specific characteristics of fermionic non-local magic, including typical random states' behavior, logarithmic scaling at quantum critical points, and magic generation during quantum quenches.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework enables scalable experimental estimation of non-local magic in large quantum processors, highlighting its potential applications in quantum computing.

title: On the Difference Between Pulsar Radio Emission Beams from the Two Poles
comment: 36 pages, 41 figures, 4 tables, ApJ, in press
summary: The long-standing assumption of symmetric radio emission beams from the two magnetic poles of pulsars is challenged by observational evidence of asymmetry and underfill. Direct testing of this symmetry remains difficult for most pulsars. As an indirect test, we collected polarization profiles of 11 interpulse pulsars observed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope, MeerKAT, and Parkes. We developed a rotating vector model incorporating aberration and retardation effects to fit the position angle swings of selected pulsars, thereby determining the intrinsic emission region corresponding to the observed pulse windows. Based on both the conal and fan beam models, we compared three key parameters-beam radius, magnetic azimuth width, and emission intensity-between the intrinsic emission regions of the main pulse and interpulse. Among the eight pulsars with a confirmed double-pole geometry, none exhibits similarity in the azimuth width. Only two show potentially similar beam radii, while six demonstrate comparable emission intensities within specific parameter spaces. These results indicate that the emission beams from the two magnetic poles of a pulsar may be generally dissimilar in size, suggesting that the physical conditions governing pair production and particle acceleration differ between the two poles. The random distribution of active emission regions further implies inhomogeneity within the polar cap, which may originate from the differences in local magnetic field structure or surface properties.

AI.tldr: This study challenges the assumption of symmetric radio emission beams from pulsars' magnetic poles by analyzing 11 interpulse pulsars and finding dissimilar emission characteristics.
AI.motivation: The research addresses the assumption that pulsar emission beams are symmetric due to the observed asymmetry and underfill in the existing data.
AI.method: Polarization profiles of interpulse pulsars were collected using multiple telescopes. A rotating vector model was developed to analyze the position angle swings and determine the intrinsic emission regions.
AI.result: Analysis revealed that none of the eight pulsars with confirmed double-pole geometry showed similar azimuth widths, with only two resembling beam radii and six comparable in emission intensities.
AI.conclusion: Results suggest pulsar emission beams from the two magnetic poles are dissimilar, indicating different governing conditions in pair production and particle acceleration, and hinting at inhomogeneities within the polar cap.

title: Low mass scalars at $e^+e-$ colliders
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures; invited review contribution to proceedings of LCWS 2025, will be published in The European Physical Journal - Plus - Focus topics
summary: I briefly discuss the search for low mass scalars at Higgs factories as well as available models that render such scalars feasible, where I focus on new developments since the review presented in arXiv:2205.09687 (see also arXiv:2504.11969 for a recent update).

title: Dark photon search status in $τ-c$ energy region
comment: Contribution to The 7th International Workshop on Future Tau-Charm Facilities (FTCF2025)
summary: The dark photon plays an important role as a portal to dark matter and has been extensively studied on both experimental and theoretical frontiers. However, as no signals have been observed, the whereabouts of the dark photon remain a long-standing open question. With the proposal of a future $τ-c$ facility, this proceeding reviews and summarizes the current experimental status of the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region, which is expected to provide a reference for future searches. The experimental status indicates that the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region remains highly promising, highlighting the requirement for larger data samples or new methods to further investigate the benchmarks related to the observed cosmic dark matter.

AI.tldr: The dark photon is a key player in dark matter research, yet remains undetected. This summary evaluates the dark photon's experimental status in the τ-c energy region and suggests future research directions.
AI.motivation: Understanding the dark photon is crucial for advancing knowledge about dark matter, an unresolved area in physics.
AI.method: This paper reviews the current experimental findings regarding dark photons in the τ-c energy region and suggests the need for larger data sets or new approaches.
AI.result: The experimental status shows that dark photons in the τ-c region still hold potential for discovery, indicating a promising avenue for future research.
AI.conclusion: Enhanced data collection or innovative methods are necessary to further probe dark photon benchmarks related to cosmic dark matter.

title: Resolving spurious topological entanglement entropy in stabilizer codes
summary: Topological entanglement entropy (TEE) is a key diagnostic of long-range entanglement in two-dimensional gapped phases of matter, but it can suffer from spurious contributions that overestimate the total quantum dimension of the underlying topological order. In this work, we identify the microscopic origin of spurious TEE and introduce a concave partition for computing the Levin-Wen TEE of translation-invariant stabilizer codes of prime-dimensional qudits. We rigorously prove that this prescription is free of spurious contributions. As a complementary probe, we study bivariate bicycle codes on a bipartite cylinder and show that the entanglement entropy depends sensitively on the cylinder circumference, revealing topological frustration of the underlying anyons.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the spurious contributions to topological entanglement entropy (TEE) and presents a method to accurately compute TEE for certain qudit codes, proving its effectiveness.
AI.motivation: To address the problem of spurious contributions to TEE that lead to overestimation of the quantum dimension in topologically ordered states.
AI.method: Introduces a concave partition for calculating Levin-Wen TEE specifically for translation-invariant stabilizer codes of prime-dimensional qudits, and proves its absence of spurious contributions.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the new TEE computation method is effective and illustrates the sensitivity of entanglement entropy in bivariate bicycle codes on a bipartite cylinder.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance the understanding of TEE in qudit systems and the underlying topological properties of anyons, providing a clearer picture of entanglement in this context.

title: Blazar flares from plasma blobs crossing the broad-line region
comment: 13 pages, 12 figures. Accepted for publication in the Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary: The blazar 3C 279 is well known for its rapid and large-amplitude variability. On 20 December 2013, the source exhibited an orphan γ-ray flare characterized by a flux-doubling timescale of a few hours, a very hard spectrum, a time-asymmetric light curve with a slow decay, and no significant optical variability. We propose a new interpretation of this event based on a two-zone scenario in which a stationary emission region produces the quiescent emission, while a second zone accelerates within the broad-line region(BLR). We compute the time-dependent radiative output of both zones with the EMBLEM code, including synchrotron, synchrotron self-Compton, and external inverse-Compton processes, as well as bulk acceleration, adiabatic expansion, and a Fokker-Planck treatment of the electron distribution. This is the first attempt to precisely model the asymmetric γ-ray flux evolution during this flare. A model with a stationary region outside the dusty torus and an accelerating plasma blob reproduces the main features of the event: a short and intense γ-ray flare with a hard spectrum and no optical counterpart. The flare results from the variation of the external photon field in the blob frame as the blob crosses the BLR and reaches its terminal Lorentz factor not far from the inner radius of the BLR. Bulk acceleration and the propagation of a plasma blob within the jet provide a natural mechanism for producing high-energy flares and asymmetric light curves without requiring an ad hoc time-dependent particle injection. The model predictsa delayed EUV/X-ray enhancement once the blob exits the BLR. No very-high-energy data are available for this event, but if γ-rays were emitted in this band, a delay would be expected with respect to the Fermi-LAT flare.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a model to explain the orphan γ-ray flare observed in blazar 3C 279 on December 20, 2013, suggesting a two-zone scenario involving stationary and accelerating emission regions.
AI.motivation: To interpret the orphan γ-ray flare in 3C 279, characterized by unique features including rapid variability, a hard spectrum, and lack of optical changes.
AI.method: The study employs a two-zone model, calculating time-dependent radiative outputs using the EMBLEM code, considering various processes like synchrotron and inverse-Compton emissions, and accounting for bulk acceleration and adiabatic expansion.
AI.result: The model successfully reproduces the flare features, explaining the flare's characteristics as a blob interacts with the broad-line region, producing a high-energy flare without direct optical changes.
AI.conclusion: The research proposes that the blob's movement through the BLR influences the observed γ-ray emissions, predicting an EUV/X-ray enhancement following the flare.

title: A theoretical account of tiny multi-Higgs vacuum expectation values from non-invertible symmetry
summary: We propose a novel mechanism to explain the naturally small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of exotic multi-Higgs fields by employing non-invertible symmetries. Specifically, we introduce an $SU(2)_L$ quartet $H_4$ and a quintet $H_5$ within the framework of the minimal Fibonacci fusion rule (FFR). This non-invertible symmetry strictly forbids the generation of tree-level VEVs for these exotic fields. However, once the symmetry is broken, these VEVs are generated radiatively at the one-loop level.This mechanism is highly minimal, as it requires no additional loop-inducing particles. We demonstrate that for various benchmark energy scales, the resulting VEVs are naturally suppressed to the order of $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$ GeV, satisfying experimental constraints from the $ρ$ parameter. Finally, we illustrate the phenomenological viability of this setup by applying it to three representative neutrino mass models: the type-III seesaw, the Dirac neutrino seesaw, and the inverse seesaw mechanisms.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a mechanism using non-invertible symmetries to explain small vacuum expectation values of exotic multi-Higgs fields with minimal extra requirements.
AI.motivation: To address the issue of small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) for exotic Higgs fields in a minimalistic framework.
AI.method: Introduces an $SU(2)_L$ quartet and quintet within the Fibonacci fusion rule, where the non-invertible symmetry forbids tree-level VEVs, allowing only one-loop generation post-symmetry breaking.
AI.result: The resulting VEVs are suppressed to approximately $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$ GeV across various energy scales, complying with experimental limits on the $ρ$ parameter.
AI.conclusion: The mechanism is phenomenologically viable, exemplified through its application to three neutrino mass models.

title: Nonlocal nonstabilizerness in free fermion models
summary: Nonlocal magic quantifies the irreducible nonstabilizerness of a bipartite quantum state after optimizing over local basis changes. We study nonlocal magic for pure fermionic Gaussian states, and derive a simple closed-form entanglement spectrum bound in terms of the singular values of the subsystem-restricted covariance matrix. We benchmark our result against simulated annealing over local Gaussian unitary transformations, which supports optimality along the full local Gaussian orbit. For states drawn from the Gaussian Haar ensemble, we show that the average nonlocal magic is extensive and determine its thermodynamic limit using random matrix theory for the appropriate circular unitary ensemble. We also study Gaussian ground states, focusing on the Kitaev chain, and find that nonlocal magic is suppressed deep in both trivial and topological phases and peaks near the critical points. Finally, we investigate Gaussian evolution via random circuits and in quenches with the XY chain. For random circuits, we find that nonlocal magic grows diffusively, while in the XY chain the XX limit reveals a striking separation between nonlocal magic and entanglement.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates nonlocal magic in pure fermionic Gaussian states, deriving a bound related to the entanglement spectrum and benchmarking it against simulated annealing for optimality across local Gaussian transformations.
AI.motivation: To better understand the structure of nonlocal magic in quantum states and establish a measurable quantification related to entanglement in quantum information theory.
AI.method: The authors derive a closed-form bound for the entanglement spectrum based on the covariance matrix's singular values, analyze the average nonlocal magic using random matrix theory, and study its behavior in various systems including the Kitaev chain and XY chain under different conditions.
AI.result: Results indicate that nonlocal magic can be expressed as extensive for states in the Gaussian Haar ensemble, shows suppression near both trivial and topological phases of the Kitaev chain, and behaves differently under random circuits as opposed to specific quantum chains.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals critical insights into the peculiarities of nonlocal magic, its correlation with entanglement, and its dynamics under various physical conditions, contributing significantly to the understanding of quantum state properties.

title: Long-term study of the gamma-ray emission of Cygnus X-3 with MAGIC and Fermi-LAT
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in JHEAP
summary: Cygnus X-3 is a microquasar composed of a compact object of unknown nature closely orbiting around a Wolf-Rayet star. The particularities of this source make it a unique case among microquasars. This fact, together with its recent establishment as a PeV particle accelerator, makes Cygnus X-3 a very interesting target for the investigation of the physical processes leading to gamma-ray production. In this work, the TeV and GeV gamma-ray emission of Cygnus X-3 is studied in order to determine its origin and constrain the properties of the system. For that purpose, a point-like analysis of 130 h of data taken with the MAGIC telescopes between 2013 and 2024 was performed, which represents the largest available sample for Cygnus X-3 at $\sim$TeV energies. Additionally, contemporary data from Fermi-LAT were also analysed to better contextualize the MAGIC observations. For a more detailed investigation of the source physics, the data were divided into three subsets according to the flaring state of the source and orbital phase. No significant detection of Cygnus X-3 is found between 0.1 and 7 TeV for any of the datasets, and differential and integral flux upper limits are reported over the long-term monitoring of the source. The Fermi-LAT fluxes can be considered compatible with previous results, taking into account the different data samples used across studies. The MAGIC upper limits presented in this work represent the most constraining ones up to date at $\sim$TeV energies. An eventual detection of Cygnus X-3 at these energies would significantly constrain the source properties, and is not unreasonable to expect given that the source has already been detected in both the GeV and PeV regimes during flaring states. Further observations of Cygnus X-3 at energies above tens of GeV would be valuable for this purpose.

AI.tldr: The study examines gamma-ray emissions from Cygnus X-3, a unique microquasar, using extensive data to determine its origin and properties but finds no significant detection in the TeV range.
AI.motivation: Investigate the physical processes behind the gamma-ray production in Cygnus X-3, particularly as it has been identified as a PeV particle accelerator.
AI.method: Conducted a point-like analysis of 130 hours of data from the MAGIC telescopes (2013-2024), complemented by Fermi-LAT data to provide context, segmenting the data based on flaring states and orbital phases.
AI.result: No significant detections were found between 0.1 and 7 TeV, but upper limits on flux were established, with MAGIC providing the most constraining limits to date.
AI.conclusion: Detection of Cygnus X-3 at TeV energies remains plausible and could greatly inform on its properties, necessitating further observations above tens of GeV.

title: Clifft: Fast Exact Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits
summary: Exact classical simulation of fault-tolerant quantum circuits remains limited by a tradeoff between exponential state vector scaling, exponential $T$-count scaling in stabilizer-rank approaches, and per-shot tracking overhead in sparse generalized stabilizer simulators.
